issues.description: The README and supplied code require several hand-collected agreement, firm-year, violation, governance, monitor-characteristic and facility-crosswalk inputs. Their producers, schemas, histories and firm-attribution rules are not supplied. identifiers_w_recid.dta is an identifier list, not the analysis panel.

PrelimDeterminants.sas creates MergeAll5 with NewCEO fields, then creates MergeAll5 again from MergeAll4 for controls, while the subsequent determinants step and export read MergeAll6. The supported exact two-line same-data working-copy repair remains proposed and unapplied; future output/sample validation is required to confirm the repaired handoff.

SAS4 constructs lev, aqi, cvar_emp, mb, roa and size and writes var1.vars_final; SAS8 consumes GLTDatFn.vars_final. The supplied files do not map those library roots, so configure a same-output alias or an unchanged handoff copy. No separate control-construction mismatch is established here; source period/history coverage remains tracked under REQ-COMPUSTAT-FUNDA.

The named BoardEx NA organization-summary candidate is present in the catalogue, but the bounded request for SAS6 fields returned unverified before reading because those requested fields were absent from the catalog. This does not establish data absence or license status.

A usable SAS runtime remains unverified. SAS4 uses PROC EXPAND, which requires SAS/ETS support; the existing startup failure does not establish component availability or license absence, and no new runtime probe was performed.
The Stata program invokes winsor2, which was not found in the bounded checked adopaths. Availability remains unresolved pending ordinary setup.
R 4.5.0 is available, but the bounded installed-package metadata probe did not find tidyverse, haven, lubridate or stringr in the queried site library.

R18 summarizes CSVs selected by directory-list positions 2, 4 and 6. The upstream Li scoring producer and FactSet transcript files are not in this package; exact names, order, required model artifacts and period remain unknown.

R20 names a 2020 KPSS archive; the current author page documents a 2025 series with updated CRSP matches and parameter estimates. Matching field names do not establish equivalence to the November 2022 handoff.

The supplied Stata excerpt saves a processed raw pull, merges it into monitor_violations, computes rd_scaled and calls winsor2, then ends at a test comment without persisting the merged result. The intended next handoff is unresolved.

R20 reads the patent_permco_permno_match_public_2020 archive into patent_match, but the supplied program never uses that object. The read is optional to the shown workflow and can be removed in a working copy if the file is unavailable.

evidence.description: The R step reads a patent-match file and a patent-level panel, joins patent data by permno and filing year, and summarizes patent counts and innovation values by rec_id-year.
evidence.quote:
# Read in Kogan et al. (2017) patents matches and data
patent_match <- read.csv(unz('patent_permco_permno_match_public_2020.csv.zip','patent_permco_permno_match_public_2020.csv'), header = T)

patent_data <- read.csv(unz('KPSS_2020_public.csv.zip','KPSS_2020_public.csv'), header = T)

# Clean up date formats
patent_data$cleanfiling_date <- as.Date(patent_data$filing_date,tryFormats = "%m/%d/%Y")

# Add filing year for summary
patent_data$filing_year <- year(patent_data$cleanfiling_date)

# Merge by permno and year
timeSeries_patents <- timeSeries2 %>%
  left_join(patent_data, by=c("lpermno"="permno","year"="filing_year")) %>%
  arrange(rec_id, year) %>%
  mutate(permnomatch = ifelse(is.na(lpermno),0,1)) %>%
  mutate(rowcount = ifelse(permnomatch==0,0,ifelse(is.na(patent_num),0,1)))

#save(timeSeries_patents,file="timeSeries_patents.RData")

# Create patent count variable and sum of innovation amounts in a given firm-year
timeSeries_patentSummarize <- timeSeries_patents %>%
  group_by(rec_id,year) %>%
  summarise(patentcount = sum(rowcount), innovation_sum = sum(xi_real,na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup()

evidence.quote:
1. Download N/DPA data from Corporate Prosecution Registry (https://corporate-prosecution-registry.com/) including: Monitor, Violation Type, Probation Length, Payment
    - Download

2. Identify GVKEYs for each observation.
    - Hand collect

    - Hand collect

evidence.description: README step 9 describes Kaal–Lacine/manual governance coding; step 10 describes Good Jobs First violation coding.
evidence.quote:
9. Create Board Changes, Business Changes, Compliance Program, Cooperation, Board Monitoring, Senior Management, Waive Rights, and Accounting Mandate variables
    - Obtain data through 2013 from Kaal & Lacine (2014) for all variables except Accounting Mandate, hand-collect by rec_id for the rest of the sample by reading N/DPA documents.
    - Merge with sample using rec_id.

10. Using Good Jobs First Violations Data, hand-collect violations data and create variable "Prior Violations of Same Type" by coding a 1 if the firm had prior violations of the same Violation Type category (as defined in Appendix A) as the N/DPA violation. Merge by rec_id.

11. For all N/DPA observations that have enough data to be in our first determinants test (193 firms), calculate a "Total Payment" variable as detailed in Appendix B for each rec_id.

evidence.description: README steps 12–15 require a hand-collected GVKEY/year series adjusted for M&A and firm-attributed violation histories.
evidence.quote:
12. Create time series of GVKEYs and years for each N/DPA-firm observation, taking into consideration M&As (as in Step 15)
    - Hand collect

13. Identify Post Infraction, Probation, and Post-Probation years
    - Post Infraction = 1 if year > Pre-Infraction Year & <= pre-DPA year, else 0
    - Probation = 1 if year > pre-DPA year & < post-DPA year
    - Post Probation = 1 if year >= post-DPA year

14. Create Treat = 1 if the N/DPA requires a Monitor and 0 otherwise

15. Hand-collect violations count (viocount_fps) from Good Jobs First Violations Data
    - Identify parent and subsidiary relationships and dates of any mergers and acquisitions through a press and general internet search
    - If the N/DPA firm acquires another firm, attribute violations by the target firm after acquisition to the N/DPA firm. 
    - If the N/DPA firm is acquired, attribute violations by the parent company after the date of acquisition to the N/DPA firm. Do not include any violations by unrelated subsidiaries of the new parent company. 
    - Account for the case in which the N/DPA firm acquires a firm that is a serial violator by including the pre-acquisition violations of the acquired subsidiary.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies CPR and primary agreement documents/DOJ releases as N/DPA sources.
evidence.quote:
1. Data on deferred and non-prosecution agreements (N/DPAs) are sourced from the Cor-
     porate Prosecution Registry (CPR), a comprehensive database of U.S. federal prose-
     cutions and deferred and non-prosecution agreements. This data can be found here:
     https://corporate-prosecution-registry.com/. [Date of download: January 9,
